verdict.rationale: Requesty issues its own gateway API keys and service-account keys for non-human entities such as apps, each with its own spend cap. Provider keys can be brought in via BYOK and held by the gateway, so clients call Requesty with a Requesty key rather than a provider key. missing for 10: explicit team-scoped key minting, explicit documentation that raw provider keys are never exposed to key holders, key-creation/rotation workflow docs, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can mint gateway-managed keys for teams and apps without exposing raw provider keys

citations.quote: Service accounts allow you create non-human entities... spend from those keys will not be tied to any user.
Each API key or service account can have its own monthly spend cap.
Bring Your Own Keys (BYOK) allows you to use your personal API keys from various providers with Requesty.
